The morning light slipped softly into the small quiet room
and filled the dusty air with a warm pale glow
It touched the edge of the old wooden table nearby
It brushed the paper notes and the cold teacup gently
A clock on the wall began to tick steadily again
The sound echoed through the silence that had gathered here
Outside a thin rain began to fall upon the street
The drops tapped the window glass like small curious fingers
I remembered a voice from childhood saying do not fear
That warning felt both gentle and heavy in my mind
The coffee cooled while I watched the water trace lines
Each line formed tiny rivers moving slowly over the pane
I wondered whether the rain knew where it would land
It seemed to choose without thought, without any careful plan
My hands rested on the table waiting for something unseen
The room held still, as if listening to the weather
A book lay open beside the mug, its pages soft
The chapter spoke of rivers finding their way through mountains
I thought of all the times I had hesitated often
Each pause had been a doorway I almost entered slowly
But the door remained shut, painted with a bright name
I read the word twice, then turned my gaze away
The rain grew thicker, turning the daylight into silver haze
Somewhere a bird began to sing against the gray sky
Its song was thin and bright, like a small thread
I wanted to follow that thread through the open window
My body stayed still, anchored by the weight of thought
The teacup held my reflection, a small stranger looking back
I smiled at that figure, remembering how easily we forget
The forgotten paths still exist beneath the ordinary ground outside
Each step I avoided becomes a road waiting for rain
The rain washes the streets until they begin to shine
A passerby paused under the awning, holding a blue umbrella
They looked at the puddles, then continued walking slowly onwards
I recognized the shape of their hesitation in my own
We are all collecting moments we cannot fully name here
The clock ticked again, marking a boundary no one sees
Time moves through the room without asking anyone for permission
The pages of the book waited patiently in the light
I thought I should read further, but my eyes drifted
They rested on the window, where the rain kept speaking
Each drop arrived as a question the glass could answer
I wondered if I could become as clear as water
If I held still enough to see the sky again
The hidden sky outside promised color through the rain softly
A child laughed, then ran across the wet pavement quickly
Their shoes splashed, sending tiny stars into the gray air
I imagined becoming one splash, brief and bright against stone
The mug steamed faintly, carrying the scent of bitter comfort
I lifted it carefully, noticing how the weight felt familiar
Warmth spread through my fingers and slowly into my chest
For a moment I felt like a house after snowfall
Quiet, full of memory, waiting for the first soft knock
The rain did not knock, but it tapped without hurry
I turned back to the page, where a sentence began
It said the traveler learns the road becomes rest slowly
I read it twice, feeling the words settle beneath me
The clock ticked, the rain answered with a soft rhythm
I noticed my breathing had matched the sound without effort
The room seemed smaller, drawn gently closer to me again
Outside, the streetlights flicked on despite the daylight remaining softly
Each lamp turned into a small moon hanging low there
The rain made halos around them, bright and trembling gently
I thought of all the people walking beneath those halos
Each one carrying a weather of their own inside them
Some storms pass quickly, while others remain for years quietly
The window glass blurred the world into a soft painting
I traced a finger along the glass, making a mark
It was temporary, already fading as the air touched it
I remembered how quickly most things dissolve when we watch
The book held its secrets still, unbothered by the weather
The teacup held the last warmth in its quiet bowl
I drank a little; the taste felt like memory again
The rain outside became a river, then a soft applause
I listened longer, letting the sound fill the empty corners
My thoughts moved slower, like leaves floating on a stream
Some became clearer, while others drifted away without a name
I accepted that not every thought needs to be kept
The room breathed with me, learning patience beside me again
The clock ticked softly, and the rain continued to speak
I wondered what morning would say if it could again
It would probably say nothing, only light and ordinary sound
I closed the book gently, letting the page fold shut
The rain thinned, leaving faint traces on the glass softly
The daylight returned, pale and cautious, like a shy guest
The street woke, with doors opening one by one softly
A bicycle wheel crossed wet asphalt, spinning in sun again
The sound of tires faded into the ordinary music outside
I opened the window, letting the damp air enter slowly
Wet stone, leaves, and distant coffee reached me now again
The world outside seemed smaller, closer, and more forgiving again
I thought about taking the walk that the rain suggested
My shoes waited by the door, hoping for me again
I stood up slowly, feeling the floor beneath my feet
The air touched my face, cool and bright and awake
The clock ticked, rain stopped, day opened wider slowly again
I walked to the door, holding morning in hands again
Outside the street shimmered, a path of small lights again
I stepped onto the sidewalk, one breath after the last
And the day began, quietly, carrying me into the unknown
